questions.q: What is the main purpose of a capstone portfolio writeup?
options: To document every single step taken, however minor
To give a stranger, like a hiring manager, a focused way to understand what was built and that you can troubleshoot a real problem
To replace the need for an architecture diagram
To prove the VPN was configured correctly
questions.explain: A strong writeup is a focused document a stranger can read in a few minutes, not a transcript of every action taken.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed as something a strong capstone writeup needs?
options: An architecture diagram
A README with design decisions
A way to verify the fix actually worked
A list of every unsuccessful troubleshooting step attempted
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly recommends against narrating every dead end — a clear, short account of the real path to the answer reads as more competent.

questions.q: What makes the example problem/fix narrative in this lesson effective?
options: It is long and highly technical
It is four plain-language sentences that show the Chapter 5 methodology actually being applied
It avoids mentioning what was actually wrong
It only describes the architecture, not the problem
questions.explain: The example narrative is short, plain-language, and demonstrates the identify/isolate/test/resolve methodology in action, which is more convincing than a vague claim.

questions.q: What should a verification step in the writeup actually show?
options: A claim that the fix worked, without evidence
The specific test, like a ping or curl, that proves the fix actually worked
A list of every device on the network
The original broken configuration only
questions.explain: Verification means showing the actual test that confirms the fix worked, not just asserting that it did.

questions.q: What course comes next in the DevOps Engineer path after IT, Networking & Cloud Fundamentals?
options: Kubernetes Orchestration
Linux Administration
Infrastructure as Code with Terraform
Docker and Containers
questions.explain: Linux Administration is next in the DevOps Engineer path, moving from the network layer onto the operating system itself.
